paragraphs: Rabbah bar Rav Huna (see there). See above, R' Abba bar Rav Huna; perhaps they are one. He was pious and humble (see above, Rava), and his curse bore fruit when he cursed Rabbah bar Rav Nahman (see there). Rav Huna gave a date to Rabbah, who gave it to his son Rava [the checked text of Sotah 49a reads Abba]. See there. After his death they brought him up with Rav Hamnuna's coffin (see there); his burial place is Kefar Alma (see R' Elazar ben Arakh). At the end of Mo’ed Katan 25a, when Rav bar Rav Huna [the checked Bavli reads Rabbah bar Huna] and Rav Hamnuna died, the eulogy that follows on 25b begins, ‘Scion of ancient ones.’ Rashi explains: this is Rabbah bar Rav Huna, a son of great men, son of Rav Huna, who was exilarch and superior to the nasi in the Land of Israel. End quotation. This wording suggests that his father Rav Huna was the exilarch. See there: Rav Huna the exilarch was in Rabbi's time and died before Rabbi and R' Hiyya. In my view this Rabbah was the son of the Babylonian Rav Huna. In the episode of the Babylonian Rav Huna’s death, Rav Hisda directs the funeral preparations and Rav Hagga takes the coffin into the burial cave. The text then recounts the deaths of Rav Hisda and Rabbah bar Rav Huna, in that order. Thus his father Rav Huna was not called exilarch; only Rav Huna of Rabbi's time was called Rav Huna the exilarch; see there. Evidence that this Rabbah was the son of the Babylonian Rav Huna, long after Rabbi, is Sanhedrin 5a: when Rabbah bar Rav Huna quarreled with the exilarch [the checked Bavli says the exilarch’s household], he said, ‘I do not hold authorization from you, but from my father and master; my father from Rav; Rav from R' Hiyya; R' Hiyya from Rabbi.’ Rashi explains: I am not subordinate to you. Tosafot there write that it is unreasonable to say Rabbah bar Rav Huna lived in Rabbi's days. Thus you see that this Rabbah bar Rav Huna does not belong to the Rav Huna the exilarch of Rabbi's time. As for Rashi's statement that Rav Huna was exilarch, see what I wrote under Rav Huna. His father Rav Huna told him, ‘My son, seize the opportunity and bless’: end of Berakhot chapter 8 and end of Nazir. Shevuot 31a has Rava bar Rav Huna; likewise Shabbat 10a, 66b, 89, end of a, 104b; Bava Batra 136, end of b. Berakhot 45b has Rava speaking to his father Rav Huna; Shabbat 121b has Rava bar Rav Huna disagreeing with his father. This is a scribal error and should read Rabbah bar Rav Huna. This Rabbah had a son called Rava bar Rabbah bar Rav Huna. Gittin 29, end of b: Rabbah bar Rav Huna said, ‘Thus my father and master said in Rav's name.’ He was with Rav Hisda on a boat. A matron used sorcery to bind them [in the checked Bavli, she binds the boat], and the sages spoke a word and released it. Shabbat 81, end of b. ‘My father and master said.’ R' Abba bar Zavda. Rav Avya the Elder asked him. Hisur the convert [חיסור in source]. He reported a teaching of Rav Ashi in Hullin 76a. He reported a teaching of Rav Giddel [Kiddushin 42a reads Rava bar Rav Huna]. Rav Hama bar Gurya was his teacher. Rav Hisda was his colleague, and his father asked him, ‘Why are you not regularly with Rav Hisda?’ See there. They sat in court all day, and R' Hiyya bar Rav of Difti spoke to them (see there). He reported a teaching of R’ Yohanan in Pesahim 91a; he asked R' Yohanan: Menahot 59b. Rav Yosef was his colleague. Rav Yitzhak bar Rav Yehudah: see above. Levi bar Huna bar Hiyya. He spoke to Mari bar Mar. Before Rav Nahman. Rav Safra came for judgment before him. Ulla spoke to him. Rav Pappa's father came before him; see there. He reported a teaching of R’ Katina. He reported teachings of Rav in Berakhot chapter 3, 25a; Shabbat 97a, 107a; Eruvin 85b; Pesahim 39a; Beitzah 25a. He raised a contradiction before Rav: Bava Batra 136, end of b. At Bava Batra 91a he reports a saying of Rav. Heilprin records another reading, “Rabbah bar Rav Yitzhak said in Rav’s name,” and attributes it to Ein Yaakov. He told Rava, or Rabbah, bar Rav Nahman, ‘Let our teacher instruct us.’ Rava was his son. Rabbah was his colleague. With Rabbah bar bar Hana, Rami bar Shmuel, Rav Yitzhak bar Rav Yehudah, and Rav Huna. He reported teachings of Shmuel in Beitzah 24a; Eruvin 49a.
